California Voters to Decide on Historic Billionaire Wealth Tax Proposal

28 Oct 2026, 08:13 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Business Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

Image: www.bbc.co.uk — Creative Commons

Key takeaways A First-of-its-Kind Policy California voters are preparing to decide on Proposition 40, a ballot measure that would levy a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of the state’s billionaires. If approved, the measure would apply to individuals with a net worth of at least $1

A First-of-its-Kind Policy

California voters are preparing to decide on Proposition 40, a ballot measure that would levy a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of the state’s billionaires. If approved, the measure would apply to individuals with a net worth of at least $1 billion who reside in California as of January 1, 2026. Proponents aim to raise approximately $100 billion to bolster the state’s healthcare system, citing expected federal funding shortfalls.

Economic Context and Public Debate

California maintains one of the world's largest economies, yet it simultaneously faces significant wealth inequality and high rates of homelessness. Supporters, including Senator Bernie Sanders and some wealthy figures like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, argue the tax is a necessary tool to address wealth concentration and fund essential public services. Conversely, critics, including California Governor Gavin Newsom, warn that the measure could prompt capital flight and drive away the state's significant income tax contributors. Some high-profile billionaires, such as Google co-founder Sergey Brin, have reportedly invested heavily in opposition efforts.

Impact and Uncertainty

The proposal has already triggered behavioral changes among some ultra-wealthy residents. Reports indicate that several billionaires have moved their primary residences out of California ahead of the potential deadline to avoid the tax. Meta, meanwhile, has adjusted its compensation structure for CEO Mark Zuckerberg, reportedly to offset the financial impact should the tax pass. Polling suggests a close contest, with recent surveys indicating a split electorate and a notable segment of undecided voters.

Practical Implications and Verification

For California voters, the decision on Proposition 40 represents a broader debate over taxation, wealth distribution, and state fiscal policy. Economists remain divided on the long-term efficacy of wealth taxes, noting that similar levies in Europe have faced administrative challenges and varying impacts on investment.

Readers can verify the specific language of the proposition, official campaign filings, and local election timelines through the California Secretary of State’s official portal or through verified state election resources.
